fullPassage:
Hello, first-year students. I'm your school counselor, Hannah Kim. How is your new school life? You may have experienced a situation where things didn't go as you expected at school. Have you ever wondered why this happens? Let's take a look at the following two cases.

The first case is about a student named Hajun. On the first day of school, Hajun's homeroom teacher introduced several school clubs. At that time, Hajun didn't have a particular preference for any of them. He thought that any indoor club would be okay since he was not an outdoor person. Can you guess what happened on the day of choice? He joined the soccer club. What made him choose soccer?

Well, a few days before submitting his application, he heard that the soccer club was so popular that half of his classmates were applying for it. This made him think that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club just because others did so. However, after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer was not for him. In the end, he regretted his decision.

Why do you think this happened? Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be excluded from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect." Following the crowd, of course, does not always lead to negative consequences, but it can lead to regret. So, how can you make your own choices? The first thing is to know what you really want. Although it might be different from your friends', don't be afraid to make your own choice. As long as you make the right choice for you, you will be happy about your decision.

Now, let's look at another case, one about Yubin. One day, Yubin told me about her first science quiz. Science was the subject that she struggled with the most. Since she wanted to get a good grade, she made a thorough study plan for herself. Yet, every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead. For instance, she cleaned her desk or texted her friends. These activities distracted her from studying, and in the end, she got a bad grade. She was frustrated that she continuously engaged in behaviors unhelpful for accomplishing her task.

When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in the short term. However, be careful! It could lead to repeated failures in certain tasks that you are not confident in doing.

If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually stop your self-handicapping.

As first-year students in high school, you'll sometimes face difficult moments. It is not unusual because everyone goes through difficult times. Even though you feel disappointed with your choices or behaviors, don't let yourself feel down. The most important thing is figuring out your own way to overcome your negative feelings. It will make your school life much more enjoyable. If you feel worried, remember that you are not alone. You have friends, teachers, and me. Good luck in this exciting new chapter of your life.

questions.passage: You may have (A)[experienced / experimented] a situation where things didn't go as you expected at school. Have you ever (B)[wondered / wandered] why this happens? Let's take a look at the (C)[following / preceding] two cases.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 예상대로 되지 않는 상황을 경험했을 수 있다. 왜 그런지 궁금해한 적이 있는가. 다음 두 사례를 살펴보자.
det.analysis:
✅ ① experienced — wondered — following ←정답
❌ ② experienced — wandered — following
❌ ③ experimented — wondered — preceding
❌ ④ experimented — wandered — preceding
(A) experienced(경험했다). experimented(실험했다)는 맥락 불일치.
(B) wondered(궁금했다). wandered(방황했다)는 맥락 불일치.
(C) following(다음의). preceding(이전의)은 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: experienced = 경험했다. wondered = 궁금했다. following = 다음의.

questions.passage: On the first day of school, Hajun's homeroom teacher introduced several school clubs. At that time, Hajun didn't have a particular (A)[preference / reference] for any of them. He thought that any (B)[indoor / outdoor] club would be okay since he was not an outdoor person. Can you guess what happened on the day of choice? He joined the soccer club. This made him think that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he (C)[signed / resigned] up for the soccer club just because others did so.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 특별한 선호가 없었다. 실내 활동을 좋아하는 사람이라 실내 동아리면 괜찮다고 생각했다. 축구 동아리에 가입했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① preference — outdoor — signed
❌ ② reference — outdoor — signed
❌ ③ preference — indoor — resigned
✅ ④ preference — indoor — signed ←정답
(A) preference(선호). reference(참고)는 맥락 불일치.
(B) indoor(실내). outdoor는 원문 'not an outdoor person' 맥락.
(C) signed up(등록했다). resigned(사직했다)는 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: preference = 선호. indoor = 실내의. signed up = 등록했다.

questions.passage: Why do you think this happened? Psychologists say that people tend to (A)[engage / disengage] in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be (B)[excluded / included] from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the (C)[crowd / individual], rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 사람들은 다른 사람이 하는 행동에 참여하는 경향이 있다. 동료 집단에서 배제되고 싶지 않다. 이런 요인이 군중을 따르게 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① engage — excluded — crowd ←정답
❌ ② engage — included — crowd
❌ ③ disengage — excluded — individual
❌ ④ engage — excluded — individual
(A) engage(참여하다). disengage(참여를 끊다)는 반대.
(B) excluded(배제되다). included(포함되다)는 맥락 불일치.
(C) crowd(군중). individual(개인)은 follow the crowd 관용 표현에 맞지 않음.
det.tip: engage in = ~에 참여하다. follow the crowd = 대세를 따르다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 축구부가 인기 있다는 소식에 특별하다고 생각했다. 하지만 가입 후 후회했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① popular(인기 있는): 원문 그대로.
❌ ② ordinary(평범한): 원문 special(특별한). 많은 친구가 지원하니 '평범하다'고 생각한다는 것은 맥락 모순. ←정답
✅ ③ regretted(후회했다): 원문 그대로.
✅ ④ tend(경향이 있다): 원문 그대로.
det.tip: special(특별한) ↔ ordinary(평범한).

det.korean: 철저한 공부 계획을 세웠다. 과학에 집중하려 했지만 다른 것을 했다. 이런 활동이 공부로부터 산만하게 했다. 좌절했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① thorough(철저한): 원문 그대로.
✅ ② concentrate(집중하다): 원문 그대로.
❌ ③ motivated(동기부여된): 원문 distracted(산만해진). 공부에서 벗어나는 맥락에서 '동기부여'는 모순. ←정답
✅ ④ frustrated(좌절한): 원문 그대로.
det.tip: distracted(산만해진) ↔ motivated(동기부여된).

det.korean: 자기 핸디캡은 성공의 장애물을 만든다. 변명을 만들게 한다. 나쁜 결과가 자존감을 낮추는 것을 방지한다. 과정에 집중하면 압박감이 줄어든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① obstacles(장애물): 원문 그대로.
✅ ② excuses(변명): 원문 그대로.
✅ ③ prevent(방지하다): 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ increase(증가시키다): 원문 ease(줄이다). 압박감을 '증가'시킨다는 것은 맥락 모순. ←정답
det.tip: ease(줄이다/완화하다) ↔ increase(증가시키다).

det.korean: 부정적인 감정을 극복하는 자신만의 방법을 찾는 것이 가장 중요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① negative(부정적인) ←정답: 실망과 좌절의 맥락에서 극복할 감정.
❌ ② positive(긍정적인): 극복 대상이 아님.
❌ ③ neutral(중립적인): 맥락 불일치.
❌ ④ temporary(일시적인): 핵심 단어가 아님.

questions.passage: Why do you think this happened? Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 군중을 따르는 현상을 ____라고 부른다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ bandwagon effect(편승 효과) ←정답: follow the crowd 현상.
❌ ① placebo effect(위약 효과): 의학 용어.
❌ ② butterfly effect(나비 효과): 연쇄 반응.
❌ ④ halo effect(후광 효과): 인상 평가.
det.tip: bandwagon effect = 편승 효과. 다수가 하면 따라하는 현상.

questions.passage: When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to __________. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping. " Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their self-esteem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과제를 잘 수행할 자신이 없으면 성공에 대한 ____하려는 경향이 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② create obstacles to success(성공에 대한 장애물을 만들다) ←정답: self-handicapping 정의.
❌ ① achieve immediate results: 자신감 부족 맥락과 불일치.
❌ ③ build strong relationships: 맥락 무관.
❌ ④ develop creative solutions: 장애물 생성과 반대.
det.tip: create obstacles to success = 성공의 장애물을 만들다. self-handicapping의 핵심.

questions.passage: Why do you think this happened? Psychologists say that people tend to <u>engage</u> in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be excluded from their peers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 engage와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 사람들은 다른 사람이 하는 행동에 참여하는 경향이 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① avoid(피하다): 반대 의미.
✅ ② participate(참여하다) ←정답: engage의 핵심 의미.
❌ ③ observe(관찰하다): 참여가 아님.
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다): 반대 의미.
det.tip: engage in = participate in = ~에 참여하다.

questions.passage: Science was the subject that she struggled with the most. Since she wanted to get a good grade, she made a <u>thorough</u> study plan for herself. Yet, every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 thorough와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 철저한 공부 계획을 세웠다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① brief(간략한): 반대 의미.
❌ ② careful(조심스러운): 유사하지만 thorough의 핵심은 '꼼꼼한/상세한'.
❌ ③ rough(대략적인): 반대 의미.
✅ ④ detailed(상세한) ←정답: thorough의 핵심 의미.
det.tip: thorough = 철저한, 상세한. a thorough study plan = 철저한 공부 계획.

questions.passage: Even though you feel disappointed with your choices or behaviors, don't let yourself feel down. The most important thing is <u>figuring out</u> your own way to overcome your negative feelings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 figuring out와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 부정적 감정을 극복하는 자신만의 방법을 알아내는 것이 가장 중요하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① giving up(포기하는): 반대 의미.
✅ ② finding out(알아내는) ←정답: figuring out의 핵심 의미.
❌ ③ running into(우연히 만나는): 맥락 무관.
❌ ④ looking after(돌보는): 맥락 무관.
det.tip: figure out = find out = 알아내다, 이해하다.

questions.passage: Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be <u>excluded</u> from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 excluded와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 사람들은 동료 집단에서 배제되고 싶지 않다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① removed(제거된): excluded와 유사.
❌ ② rejected(거부된): excluded와 유사.
✅ ③ accepted(받아들여진) ←정답: excluded(배제된)의 반의어.
❌ ④ avoided(피해진): excluded와 유사한 방향.
det.tip: excluded(배제된) ↔ accepted(받아들여진/포함된).

questions.passage: Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more <u>encouraged</u> to try to do the challenging tasks.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 encouraged와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 도전적인 과제를 시도하도록 더 격려받을 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① motivated(동기부여된): encouraged와 유사.
❌ ② inspired(영감받은): encouraged와 유사.
✅ ③ discouraged(의기소침해진) ←정답: encouraged(격려된)의 반의어.
❌ ④ empowered(힘을 얻은): encouraged와 유사.
det.tip: encouraged(격려된) ↔ discouraged(의기소침해진).

questions.passage:
(A) She decided to <u>work</u> harder on her math skills this semester.
(B) The new medicine seems to <u>work</u> well for her headaches.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 work이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (A) She decided to work harder on her math skills this semester. (B) The new medicine seems to work well for her headaches.

det.korean: (A) 이번 학기 수학 실력을 위해 더 노력하기로 했다. (B) 새 약이 두통에 효과가 있는 것 같다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 노력하다 — (B) 작동하다/효과가 있다 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 노력하다 — (B) 일하다
❌ ③ (A) 일하다 — (B) 작동하다/효과가 있다
❌ ④ (A) 일하다 — (B) 일하다
(A) work harder on = ~에 더 노력하다. 본문: This might work in the short term.
(B) work well = 효과가 있다/작동하다.
det.tip: work (동사) = 노력하다 / 효과가 있다. 다의어.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"a strong desire or inclination to do something, especially something unwise or wrong"

det.korean: 특히 현명하지 않거나 잘못된 것을 하고 싶은 강한 욕구나 경향.
det.analysis:
❌ ① obstacle(장애물): 욕구가 아님.
✅ ② temptation(유혹) ←정답: 영영 정의에 정확히 부합.
❌ ③ consequence(결과): 욕구가 아님.
❌ ④ preference(선호): 잘못된 것에 대한 욕구는 아님.
det.tip: temptation = 유혹. 본문 맥락: 공부 대신 다른 것을 하게 되는 유혹.

questions.passage: Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the __________ (challenge) tasks.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 과정에 집중하면 도전적인 과제를 시도할 용기가 생긴다.
det.analysis: the __________ (challenge) tasks: 명사 tasks를 수식하는 형용사 필요. challenge → challenging(도전적인).
det.tip: challenging(형용사) = 도전적인. the challenging tasks = 도전적인 과제들.

questions.passage: These activities distracted her from studying, and in the end, she got a bad grade. She was frustrated that she continuously engaged in behaviors __________ (help) for accomplishing her task.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 공부에서 산만해져 나쁜 성적을 받았다. 과제 달성에 도움이 되지 않는 행동에 계속 참여한 것에 좌절했다.
det.analysis: behaviors __________ (help) for accomplishing: 과제 달성에 '도움이 되지 않는' 행동. help → unhelpful(도움이 되지 않는).
det.tip: unhelpful = 도움이 되지 않는. un- 접두사로 반대 의미. 문맥상 부정 형용사 필요.

questions.passage: Also, people don't want to be excluded from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to __________, rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이런 심리적 요인이 사람들을 자신의 판단보다 ____하게 만든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① follow the crowd(군중을 따르다) ←정답: bandwagon effect의 핵심.
❌ ② stand on your own(혼자 서다): 반대 개념.
❌ ③ break the rules(규칙을 어기다): 맥락 무관.
❌ ④ miss the point(요점을 놓치다): 맥락 무관.
det.tip: follow the crowd = 대세를 따르다. bandwagon effect의 정의.

questions.passage: If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider __________. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the challenging tasks.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자기 핸디캡을 하는 이유는 결과를 과정보다 더 중요하게 여기기 때문이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ the results more important than the process ←정답: self-handicapping의 원인.
❌ ① 과정이 동등하게 중요: 해결책이지 원인이 아님.
❌ ② 교사와 학생: 맥락 무관.
❌ ④ 결과가 덜 중요: 원인의 반대.
det.tip: 결과 > 과정 → self-handicapping 원인. 과정에 집중 → 해결.
